Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and legal review we need a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) / cross-border data transfer summary to satisfy our GDPR team. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation of where customer data (logs, input text, embeddings) may be transferred/stored (regions and subprocessor locations).
- Copies of SCCs you use or confirmation you will sign our baseline SCCs.
- Whether you do any persistent storage of raw customer content outside the EEA and how you isolate EU customer data.
- Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM use, key custody model.
- Any DPIA you have performed or a short statement about GDPR risk mitigations.

If you have a short one-page TIA summary and the DPA + SCCs or a link to the signed SCCs, that would speed up review. We may need a brief tech call with your security lead if anything is unclear.

Can you share by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Anna

Marissa —

Summary answers below (short form) — Laura / Infra please correct if I get any detail wrong and attach the TIA PDF.

1) Hosting & processing locations: primary control plane and customer metadata live in EU (Frankfurt, eu-central-1) for customers who select EU region; hosted offering defaults to multi-region US, but we provide EU-dedicated regions for customers who require it. Transient inference compute can occur in regions that include US and EU depending on routing policy. Persistent storage of customer content (for customers who elect to retain logs/embeddings) is configurable and can be limited to EU-only when requested.

2) Subprocessors: we use the following (representative):
   - CloudInfraCo (AWS eu-central-1) — hosting (DE)
   - S3-Storage-Partner — object store (IE)
   - MonitoringOps Ltd — telemetry (IE)
   - VectorIndexCorp — embeddings store (US) (only for customers who opt into managed embeddings)

3) Encryption & keys: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. Customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM). For BYOK, keys never leave customer-managed KMS and Redwood stores only key identifiers.

4) DPIA / privacy review: Privacy & Trust completed an internal DPIA for our inference product in 2025; we have a one-page executive summary (redwood-tia-eu-summary-20260120.pdf). We also maintain processing records and a published DPA.

I recommend we attach: Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf, Redwood_SCCs_signed.pdf, redwood-tia-eu-summary-20260120.pdf. Laura — can you confirm the subprocessor country list and add any nuance about cache/KV lifetime?

-Rishi

Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Adding technical detail:

- Cache/KV lifetime: default KV cache TTL is 24 hours; prefix/prompt caching can be configured down to session-only. For EU-dedicated customers we set cache retention to session-only by default.
- Persistent embeddings: stored only if the customer opts into managed embeddings; retention and location are configurable and we provide tooling to purge.
- Access controls: RBAC with least privilege, audit logs stored for 180 days (configurable enterprise retention up to 7 years).
- Logs: request logs are pseudonymized for production usage; full raw inputs are retained only when customer enables log retention.
- DPIA note: the DPIA flagged residual cross-border risk when using third-party index services; we mitigate with contractual SCCs and technical isolation (VPC peering, private link).

I've uploaded the one-page TIA summary and the DPA/SCCs to the shared drive.
